s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monocular vision loss with associated eyelid and forearm pain, numbness, and erythema
salient_findings: Pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of the eyelids and forearm
Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, corneal haze, and restricted motility
Serous retinal detachment and macular whitening
key_facts: Obese man in his mid-30s
No prior systemic or ocular disorders
Heavy alcohol consumption the night prior
Took 2 buprenorphine hydrochloride/naloxone hydrochloride pills
Denied any trauma
Visual acuity: No light perception in right eye, 20/20 in left eye
Intraocular pressure: 37 mm Hg in right eye, 21 mm Hg in left eye
Creatinine level: 2.2 mg/dL
Creatine kinase level: 29,320 U/L
Periorbital soft-tissue swelling on noncontrast computed tomography
Severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography
Delayed choroidal filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute monocular vision loss with associated eyelid and forearm pain, numbness, and erythema
salient_findings: Pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of the eyelids and forearm
Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, corneal haze, and restricted motility
Serous retinal detachment and macular whitening
key_facts: Obese man in his mid-30s
No prior systemic or ocular disorders
Heavy alcohol consumption the night prior
Took 2 buprenorphine hydrochloride/naloxone hydrochloride pills
Denied any trauma
Visual acuity: No light perception in right eye, 20/20 in left eye
Intraocular pressure: 37 mm Hg in right eye, 21 mm Hg in left eye
Creatinine level: 2.2 mg/dL
Creatine kinase level: 29,320 U/L
Periorbital soft-tissue swelling on noncontrast computed tomography
Severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography
Delayed choroidal filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography

differentials: vascular malformation causing carpal tunnel syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's sudden vision loss in one eye, no light perception in the right eye, and findings such as delayed retinal arterial filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography, along with severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography, are highly suggestive of central retinal artery occlusion.

rejected.label: glaucoma
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated intraocular pressure, the primary presentation of sudden vision loss and specific findings on imaging studies points more directly to a vascular issue rather than glaucoma.

rejected.label: retinal detachment
rejected.why: Although serous retinal detachment is noted, it is not the primary diagnosis that explains all the key findings, especially the sudden onset and the specific vascular perfusion issues seen on Fluorescein Angiography.

rejected.label: proptosis
rejected.why: Proptosis refers to the protrusion of the eyeball, which is not the primary issue here; the focus is on vision loss and vascular issues within the eye.

rejected.label: optic neuritis
rejected.why: Optic neuritis typically presents with pain on eye movement and decreased vision, but the extensive vascular and retinal findings in this case are more indicative of a vascular occlusion than inflammation of the optic nerve.
